author: cskiraly
content:
Hi everyone,
I know I was a bit silent yesterday, sorry for that, but I had to work a bit on a few pieces. Here is what I was (and I am working on),

- I see some confusion around SEACAST. I had several calls explaining it (thanks to everyone reaching out) and came to the idea that I need to improve the description :-). Not really the specs, but how they are laid out in the repository and in files. So that’s one thing ongoing, soon to be pushed.
- My proposal for payload broadcast (and also for handling the BAL) has been out for quite some time. I see that in a narrow reading some think SEACAST was developed just for that, and for that it’s a huge spec. That’s a misunderstanding. It was developed for various broadcast and sampling services. Here you can find the version for proof broadcast: https://notes.ethereum.org/@cskiraly/fast-leanvm-proof-broadcast-review  <@439032863904628745>  this might be interesting for you!
- The above also comes with a smaller spec, because a large spec is frightening. SEACAST was developed to handle also sampling. It is rooted in my FullDAS work (and many of my works from before that), which handled sampling (together with its edge case of sampling where you need the “total sample”, which happens to be exactly broadcast). Anyway, we don’t need sampling now for these experiments, and you might not want to change PeerDAS just now. So there is a profile, a smaller spec carved out from te full specs for the case of attestation aggregate broadcast: https://notes.ethereum.org/@cskiraly/seacast-aggregate-proofs . It is defined over the Waggle binding, although it would work over other bindings too.
- As an implementer, some might prefer implement the whole thing, thus haveing one codebase, and use it for 1-2-3 services. Others might take these lean profiles and build those out, narrow. It is not for me to say which is your way, I think both works. My branches are doing the full thing because I also use them for research.

author: cskiraly
content:
- I’m also working on a new version of the Prysm code that is easy to adopt to different bindings. SEACAST has 4 bindings defined (Gossipsub, Waggle, libp2p streams, QUIC). “Why is this good”, some people were asking in the calls. It is because in protocol design one of the challenges is capturing the boundaries, the APIs, and the untold assumptions around these. By having more bindings you ensure that you understand what you rely on and what are these boundaries. Ii is common practice in networking. Useful even if we end up not using it.
- There are some other points I’m working on, but this is getting long. Another update will follow

author: barnabasbusa
content:
<@&1573153274616356916> we're aiming to launch **pq-devnet-1 tomorrow (Nov 27)** 🚀

Main thing under test: **staggered aggregation** (consensus-specs `4595f0fc`) with every client on **leanVM bindings v0.19.0** (`351f7ae4`), in-process, no sidecar. Proofs from other leanVM revisions won't verify, so no older versions.

Notes: https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/pq-devnet-1

Please prep today:
- Push a `pq-devnet-1` branch; the image builder turns it into `ethpandaops/<client>:pq-devnet-1` with your stock Dockerfile. Have images: teku, lodestar, grandine, ethlambda, silver. Missing: lighthouse, prysm, nimbus.
- Bump to leanVM v0.19.0 (`MAX_CACHED_BOTTOM_TREES` → `DEFAULT_BOTTOM_TREE_CACHE_SIZE`).
- Go through "Client requirements from pq-devnet-0" on the notes page: XMSS cache loading + fallback, next bottom tree built in the background, parallel signing with publish-on-sign, 32-byte pubkeys in the beacon API, range/envelope sync.
- Test interop locally with `.github/tests/pq-devnet-1.yaml` on the ethereum-package `pq` branch.
- Update your row in the readiness table, or reply here with branch + status.

Keys: still not on Manu's derivation pattern, we're letting that cook a bit longer. Keys are derived from BLS the same way as pq-devnet-0. VRF trees change (leaves commit to secrets, `b5d422b2`), so genesis VRF roots and `.vrf` files are new; we'll publish them before launch.

Once devnet-1 is up and finalizing, we'll shut down pq-devnet-0.
